response.rationale: The presentation best fits cervicogenic dizziness: recurrent vertigo and unsteadiness without vestibular or central localizing features, negative HINTS, normal vascular imaging and hemodynamics, and symptoms provoked by movement/position. Orthostatic intolerance is less supported because vital signs were normal and episodes lasted days to weeks.

rejected.why: Atherosclerosis is incidental; CTA stenosis was overestimated and TCD hemodynamics were normal.
Carotid stenosis was overestimated and there was no hemodynamic compromise or acute lesion.
No orthostatic vital sign changes were documented and prolonged vertiginous episodes are not typical of orthostatic intolerance.
Vertebrobasilar insufficiency is excluded by normal TCD, no recent MRI lesions, and low central vestibular probability.
Vestibular disorder is unlikely given negative HINTS, low vestibular probability, and ineffective symptomatic treatment.
Chronic white matter changes are non-specific and not accompanied by recent vascular lesions or a central vestibular pattern.
No acute or recent cerebrovascular lesions were found and the presumed stroke was not confirmed on imaging.
